feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (no prior race evidence for the controller) showed every trial on all three development tracks ending off track after exactly one line-loss event, with max_error about 0.061 m, progress 0.11 to 0.16, and finish rate 0. Steering oscillation was low (0.08 to 0.16) and rms_error small (about 0.03), so the failure is a single excursion past the 0.06 m off-track floor, not jitter. The floor is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which at body_width 0.12 gives 0.06 m, so the sensor layout is the lever. The 8 cm span in this proposal is designed to keep tape under a sensor on bends. If the next race shows line_loss_events at 0 and max_error below 0.06 on the tight bends while rms_error stays near 0.03 on gentle bends, keep the span at ±0.04 and move on to drivetrain. If line losses persist on the tightest bends (first loss still occurs and max_error still reaches 0.06), widen the outer sensors further. If rms_error rises on gentle bends with losses gone, the span is now too coarse, so narrow the inner spacing rather than the outer reach.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is still at least 1 per run on the tightest bends (iteration 1 with the 8 cm span), widen the outer sensors to about x = ±0.05 with inner sensors at ±0.025, since iteration 0 showed the 6 cm span failing with one excursion per run.

If line losses are gone but rms_error rises above about 0.04 on gentle bends (iteration 0 rms_error was about 0.03), keep the outer sensors at ±0.04 and reduce wheel_track to 0.10 m for sharper turning only if completion_time remains a limit, since iteration 0 showed low steering oscillation (0.08 to 0.16), which points to a responsiveness limit, not jitter.

If the signal jitters as tape crosses between sensors (steering_oscillation rising well above the iteration 0 range of 0.08 to 0.16), test sensor_size 0.016 m, which overlaps neighbouring sensors more and smooths the centroid, and check whether rms_error improves.
